data.narrative:
GITAI, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $129M+ to date, is evaluated against a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ). The primary peer set includes Hadrian, Agile Robots, and Nimble Robotics, all at Series C stage.

Two triangulation methods anchor the valuation. Stage-progression applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $129M raised proxy, yielding $219M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same-stage comparables produces a $1.0B midpoint, with a range of $1.0B to $1.6B. The peer set reflects heterogeneity: Hadrian stands at $1.6B while Agile Robots and Nimble Robotics each value at $1.0B.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $186M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $610M. The wide spread reflects material variance between the raised-proxy and peer-median approaches. Stage-progression is conservative, anchored directly to capital deployment; peer-median is elevated, reflecting the strong capital efficiency and growth multiples commanded by later-stage robotics platforms. Key uncertainties include GITAI's relative revenue scale and unit economics versus the peer cohort, as well as near-term commercialization trajectory. A post-Series C valuation likely settles in the $400M–$900M range, contingent on revenue inflection and market conditions.
